pairs.subject: copy-quality-gates
pairs.evidence: src/features/teams/sub_factory/passport/improve/standards.ts:31 User-facing action labels and hints are written as English object literals in a .ts data file, outside the i18n catalog, and ImprovePopover renders them, so no catalog-walking copy gate extracts them and none declares them out of scope: a coverage hole with a green light over it.

techniques.evidence: src/features/teams/sub_factory/passport/improve/standards.ts:32 The technique says copy outside the catalog (literals in code) must be extracted through the same pipeline or declared out of scope. This hint is rendered at ImprovePopover.tsx:132 ({a.hint}) and is neither. The same pattern appears in goldenStandard.ts labels, levels.ts titles and notes, and ImproveCell.tsx:74 title literals.

src/features/teams/sub_factory/passport/improve/goldenStandard.ts:28 This context consumes copy; it is not where a copy contract, brief or fact sheet would live. Its 'golden standard' is a repo-readiness rubric, not a copy standard.

pairs.registryProposal: rendered-string-extraction's 'copy outside the catalog' rule could name the common UI-code shape directly: typed config arrays of {label, hint} objects in .ts files. JSX-text lint rules structurally miss these, and they are the dominant escape route in a React codebase whose JSX is already lint-gated.
